t: Maximum Number of Balls in a Box - Counting Digit Sums
o: Ball numbers run from lowLimit to highLimit inclusive; each ball is dropped into the box numbered by its digit sum (ball 321 goes to box 3+2+1 = 6, ball 10 to box 1), and we must report the population of the fullest box. For lowLimit = 5, highLimit = 15 the digit sums are 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 - boxes 5 and 6 receive two balls each, so the answer is 2. The constraints are gentle: at most 100000 balls, and any number up to 100000 has digit sum at most 45 (from 99999), so a fixed array of 46 counters captures every possible box label and no hashing is needed. Each ball therefore requires only work proportional to its number of digits; the only mild refinement available is computing consecutive digit sums incrementally instead of peeling every digit each time.
k: Digit sums act as a hash with a tiny codomain: for inputs up to 10^5 every box label lies in 1..45, so a fixed-size counter array replaces a hash map entirely.
Consecutive numbers allow reuse via ds(x) = ds(x / 10) + x % 10 - the digit sum of x comes in O(1) from an already-computed smaller value.

a.i: For every ball number, peel digits off with modulo and division, increment the counter bucket for the resulting box label, and track the maximum along the way. Straightforward, allocation-free, and far inside the limits.
s: For each x from lowLimit to highLimit, compute its digit sum by repeated mod/divide.
Increment that bucket and keep a running maximum.
a.t: O((highLimit - lowLimit + 1) * log10(highLimit)) - each number contributes one step per digit.

a.i: Digit sums of nearby integers overlap heavily: dropping the last digit of x yields a number whose digit sum is already known. Fill the table ds[x] = ds[floor(x/10)] + x%10 for every x starting from 1 - starting anywhere else would leave prefix entries undefined - then count only balls inside the requested range. Each lookup becomes O(1), trading O(highLimit) memory for a smaller per-ball constant.
s: Allocate a ds table over 0..highLimit plus counters for labels 0..45.
Fill ds[x] = ds[x // 10] + x % 10 in increasing order of x starting at 1.
For each x within [lowLimit, highLimit], increment counter[ds[x]] and track the maximum.
a.t: O(highLimit - lowLimit + 1) - constant work per ball after the O(1) memo lookup.

w: Either approach passes instantly; say out loud that the output domain has only ~45 possible boxes before choosing a data structure - it shows you bound the problem before coding (a hash map also works but buys nothing here). Pitfalls: forgetting that the maximum digit sum for this constraint range is 45 (size your fixed arrays accordingly or use a map); off-by-one on the inclusive highLimit; and in JavaScript, using integer division consistently rather than relying on float division. Follow-ups: also report which box wins under ties, handle ranges up to 10^18 (digit DP over the distribution instead of enumeration), or count how many boxes hold exactly q balls.
